Heroes:

Skyscraper -  I like the theme of hard size and maybe her innate power is something like discard x cards deals one target x damage.  If that's not the innate power maybe that's a one shot and if that's the one shot her innate power deals with drawing.   To some degree, I would see her having to be a bit of a tank since I imagine being large would cause her to receive a lot of the damage.  Also some cards would manipulate environments duets her size whether that's because chucks an environment card with HP at someone or she destroys an environment due to her size again.  

 

Captian Cosmic -  I see some mix between silver surfer and green latern.   His innate power or his cards cause environment manipulation.  I see him having cards that allow damage to come to him and on his turn he deals one target X damage.  Another idea is maybe he has card that requires others to discard so he can perform a powerful abilities.  

Villains:

I imagine seeing a Galactus type villain.  Part of his ability being that destroyed environments cards go under him and after he hits H cards he flips.   I would imagine his flipped side being destructive enough that you want to defeat him before that happens otherwise you have quite the uphill battle. 

 

Environments:

posts.cooked: Having seen the V5 in action now, I find myself suspicious of the assumption that Tantrum can be taken as predictive of what Skyscraper will do.  A lot of the nemeses' abilities don't seem to have much in particular to do with their counterpart.  Equity for instance didn't seem to do anything that particularly messes with Naturalist, nor Man-Grove with Nightmist, nor Zhu Long with Fixer; the only ones I can think of which did seem to correspond were Calypso, The Crackjaw Crew, and to a fairly slight extent the Radioactivist.  Yes we could look at Empyreon and assume that Captain Cosmic's shtick must be making villains damage themselves, but it's also possible that the nemeses were just designed to do general villain-target things, and to do them slightly better if their storyline-based enemy happens to be in play.  Tantrum might be designed to ironically reflect Sky the way Calypso does Ra, but she also might just be designed to give the Ermine deck environment destruction for purely mechanical reasons.
